summary: Register an OAuth App in your GitHub settings. It is instant: no review, no waiting. Org-owned data may need an owner to approve the app.

difficulty.label: Self-serve
difficulty.rationale: The registration page describes no review or approval step; the app is created when you click Register.

effort.basis: Our estimate from the number of form fields and copy steps. No source states a setup time (Composio's guide shows only a 7-minute reading time).

wait.statement: No review or approval step is mentioned on the registration page. Access to private organization resources can additionally require an organization owner to approve the app.
wait.headline: No review
wait.note: Register the app and use it right away. Organization owners may need to approve it for their repos.

composio_managed.note: Composio's Github toolkit page lists OAuth2 and says 'Composio-managed OAuth available.' So a developer can connect users without registering their own provider app first; register your own only for your own branding, scopes or rate limits.

requirements.text: A GitHub account. You can register the app under your user or under an organization.
Three inputs are implied by the form: application name, homepage URL and authorization callback URL. Description is optional.

scopes_and_access.text: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps; each app can have up to 10 callback URLs.
Ask only for scopes the tools need. Composio's example uses broad scopes (repo, user, gist, notifications, project, workflow, codespace) and presents them as an example, not a recommendation.

gotchas.text: Stay in 'OAuth Apps', not 'GitHub Apps' or personal access tokens - they are different products with different setup.
The client secret is shown only once; if lost, generate a new one and update Composio.
Do not put internal URLs or other sensitive data in the app's public fields.
'Expire user access tokens' is on by default; turn it off only if your auth code does not support short-lived tokens.
New GitHub organizations have OAuth app access restrictions turned on by default, so your app may be blocked for org-owned repos until an owner approves it. Members can request that approval.
If your product needs to act without a signed-in user, GitHub says GitHub Apps can act independently of a user; OAuth apps cannot. This guide covers OAuth apps only.

steps.title: Open Developer settings
steps.detail: Profile picture (top right) > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps. If the app should belong to a team, do this from the organization's settings instead.

steps.title: Get the callback URL from Composio first
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for GitHub with 'Use your own developer credentials' and copy the redirect URI it shows. Do not trust a URL in a screenshot - Composio's guide says the screenshot is older than the current URI.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.detail: New OAuth App > enter name, homepage URL, optional description, and the authorization callback URL. Leave Device Flow off unless you need headless auth. Click Register application.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and generate a client secret
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID. Generate a client secret and store it immediately in a secret manager or environment variable.
steps.why_not_agent: The secret must go straight into your secret store; do not paste it into chats or commit it.

steps.title: Paste credentials into Composio and connect
steps.detail: Enter client ID and secret in the auth config, then use Connect Account with a test user ID and authorize on GitHub.

blockers.likely_cause: The callback URL in GitHub differs from the redirect URI in your current Composio auth config.
blockers.fix: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio auth config and paste it as the callback URL in GitHub, exactly.
blockers.escalate_when: It still fails after an exact match - check which environment/auth config you are using.

blockers.symptom: Authorization works but private org repos are missing
blockers.likely_cause: An organization owner has to approve access before the app can reach private organization resources.
blockers.fix: Use the Request button on the consent screen's organization section and ask an owner to approve.
blockers.escalate_when: The org restricts third-party app access and no owner responds.

review_process.text: No GitHub review step is described for registering an OAuth app; the page we read ends at 'Register application'. Organization owners may still need to approve it per org.

next_actions: Register the app and copy credentials (about 10-20 min hands-on).
Connect a test account in Composio and run one simple GitHub tool to confirm scopes.

agent_can: Explain the form fields and fetch the redirect URI from your Composio auth config via API.
Create the Composio auth config once you provide the client ID and secret through a secure input.
Run a test tool call after connection.
you_must: Sign in to GitHub and register the OAuth app.
Ask an org owner to approve access if needed.
